2. Inter-domain geometry — all domain pairs, every structure

All 3 ordered domain pairs are reported for each of the 5 structures, so that a pair which does not move is as visible as one that does. Centroid distance (Å) is the Cα centroid separation; it is rotation-blind. Contacts counts residue pairs with any Cα within 10 Å across the two domains; it has no geometric failure mode and is the measure used to call open vs closed. Coverage is the percentage of each domain actually present in the model — a pair with low coverage gives a distance that cannot be compared with the full-length one.

3. Predicted aligned error

AlphaFold v6 PAE for all 2527 residues, block-averaged to a 200×200 grid. Dark blocks on the diagonal are confidently placed units; a bright off-diagonal block means the two units' relative position is not predicted. A bright off-diagonal block does not distinguish a two-state switch from a floppy linker — that is why the geometry above, not the PAE, decides open vs closed.

4b. The ten closest sequence homologs in the human proteome

phmmer (HMMER 3.4) of the canonical LRRK2 sequence against all 20,431 reviewed human SwissProt entries, E-value threshold 10−3; the protein itself is excluded. These are the proteins whose structures are worth borrowing from, and whose mutation literature transfers most readily.

10M3K10Q0277986.66.0e-2533.957.628311.2Mitogen-activated protein kinase kinas
How to read these numbers. Bit score is the alignment score on a log2 scale, independent of database size: it is the number to rank by. Above ~50 means real homology, above ~200 means unambiguous homology, and above ~1000 over near-full coverage means a close paralogue. E-value is how many hits this good would be expected by chance in these 20,431 sequences; 10−3 was the cutoff, and 0.0 means below floating-point resolution, not zero evidence. It depends on database size, so it is not comparable across searches of different databases. % identity is counted over aligned columns only, and % similarity adds conservative substitutions. Below about 25–30% identity — the “twilight zone” — identity alone stops discriminating homology from chance, which is exactly where the bit score and E-value still do. % query covered is aligned columns over the full query length: a high bit score with low coverage (ABL1 and BTK against the SRC-family kinases, ~39–66%) means one shared domain matched, not the whole protein — borrow a kinase domain from such a hit, never an inter-domain arrangement.

dbNSFP indexes only substitutions reachable by a single nucleotide change — about 31% of all amino-acid substitutions are not, and those have no row here. V→F, for instance, needs two changes. The mutation is still fully computed in sections 6 to 8; only the clustering, which is built on the dbNSFP variant table, cannot place it.

A GOF mutation landing in the tolerant cluster is not a failure: every predictor in the panel scores loss of function, so gain-of-function variants are systematically called benign. That is a known, structural limitation of the panel rather than noise.

9. Literature review

9.0 Five papers that establish the conformational states, at the level of the JAK literature

The benchmark for this project is the set of four JAK papers that between them report the inter-domain arrangement experimentally and model the transition: Lupardus 2014 (the TYK2 JH2–JH1 crystal), Glassman 2022 (full-length JAK by cryo-EM), Shan 2014 (the JH2–JH1 autoinhibitory interface from MD, D. E. Shaw Research) and Ayaz 2019 (full-length JAK2 in active and inactive forms, D. E. Shaw Research — a bioRxiv preprint with no peer-reviewed version). The five below are the equivalent for this protein, graded by how directly they answer the question: A = reports or models two or more distinct inter-domain arrangements of this protein; B = one arrangement experimentally, or the transition approached indirectly.

  • tier A Deniston CK et al., Nature 2020;588:344-349. Structure of LRRK2 in Parkinson's disease and model for microtubule interaction. PMID 32814344
    Cryo-EM of LRRK2 and a model for microtubule interaction: the first full inter-domain architecture.
  • tier A Watanabe R et al., Cell 2020;182:1508-1518.e16. The In Situ Structure of Parkinson's Disease-Linked LRRK2. PMID 32783917
    The IN SITU structure of LRRK2 inside cells - the arrangement as it actually occurs, including the filament form.
  • tier A Myasnikov A et al., Cell 2021;184:3519-3527.e10. Structural analysis of the full-length human LRRK2. PMID 34107286
    Structural analysis of full-length human LRRK2: the autoinhibited, closed inter-domain arrangement of the whole protein.
  • tier A Zhu H et al., Science 2023;382:1404-1411. Rab29-dependent asymmetrical activation of leucine-rich repeat kinase 2. PMID 38127736
    Rab29-dependent ASYMMETRICAL activation - two different inter-domain arrangements within one assembly.
  • tier A Villagran Suarez A et al., Cell 2026;189:6460-6473.e7. The structural basis for LRRK2's activation and autoinhibition. PMID 42575089
    The structural basis for LRRK2's activation and autoinhibition: the open and closed states and the transition, 2026.

9.1 Further notes on the conformations: is there a real open and a real closed state?

What is actually known about this protein occupying more than one inter-domain arrangement.

  • The DFG motif is a conformational switch driving LRRK2 activation; Y2018 in the DFGψ motif acts as a brake, and Y2018F is hyperactive, phenocopying G2019S — link checked this session
  • Molecular dynamics reports that G2019S stabilises the DYGI loop and promotes the closed kinase conformation checked this session
    IMPORTANT: that 'closed' is the intra-domain active-site conformation, not the inter-domain arrangement measured here. The two senses must not be conflated — see open_close/open_close_inf.md.
  • Conformation and dynamics of the kinase domain drive subcellular location and activation of LRRK2 — link checked this session

9.2 Mutations

Primary reports behind the substitutions computed in section 6.

  • G2019S is the commonest genetic cause of Parkinson's disease; I2020T is DFG-adjacent; R1441C/G/H are in the Roc GTPase domain and Y1699C in COR checked this session
  • The G2019S mutation imparts resiliency to kinase inhibition — link
    A GOF mutation that also reduces inhibitor sensitivity — the same coupling of activation and resistance seen for SHP2 E76K.

9.3 Drugs and drug resistance

Why the conformational question is a therapeutic question for this protein.

  • LRRK2 kinase inhibitors are in clinical development for Parkinson's; a G2019S-selective inhibitor has been reported to abrogate mitochondrial DNA damage — link checked this session

9.4 Associated disease

  • Autosomal-dominant Parkinson's disease; also associated with Crohn's disease and leprosy susceptibility

10. Caveats — read before using any number here

1. Some ΔΔG magnitudes are repulsion, not free energies. The protocol repacks only an 8 Å shell around the mutated site and applies no global FastRelax (that choice buys ~100k variants/hour instead of ~11 minutes per structure). When a larger side chain cannot be accommodated by local repacking alone, the Lennard-Jones repulsive term dominates and the result is an arbitrary large positive number. Any |ΔΔG| above 25 REU is flagged with ⚠ and should be read as “sterically impossible without backbone relaxation”, not as a measured energy. Affected here: G2019S, Y1699C.
2. “Open” and “closed” here mean the inter-domain arrangement. The same two words are used in the kinase literature for at least three other things: the G-loop over the ATP site (a few Å), the DFG-in/DFG-out flip (~10 Å), and the WPD loop in phosphatases. A paper reporting that a mutation “stabilises the closed conformation” may well be talking about the active site, not the domain arrangement computed here. See open_close/open_close_inf.md in this repository for the measured comparison of the senses.
3. The predictor panel is blind to gain of function. Every member scores loss of function or loss of stability. A constitutively activating mutation is therefore expected to score benign, and does. Cluster membership is evidence about tolerance, never about direction of effect.
4. Renumbering is sequence-based. Template and experimental coordinates arrive in author numbering; each is mapped to canonical UniProt positions by the offset maximising sequence identity, and the achieved identity is reported in section 1. An offset with low identity means the mapping is unreliable and every per-residue number from that model with it.
5. Coverage limits the geometry. A centroid distance computed from a partial domain is not comparable with one from the complete domain. Pairs where either domain is under 70% present are marked with * in section 2.
